subject: Security exhibit: scope, evidence cadence and pen-test access
messages:
From: Alice Byrne <alice.byrne@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Grant <tom.grant@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit + audit scope questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for sending the order form earlier. Our security team reviewed the attached MSA + security exhibit and had a few open items before procurement can sign:

- We need confirmation Redwood will share the SOC 2 Type II report (most recent) and a high-level pen-test summary.
- The exhibit currently includes "unrestricted audit access" language — can you clarify what that means in practice (on-site interviews, production access, logs, copies of data)?
- What evidence cadence are you proposing (monthly artifact drop, quarterly report, ad-hoc on request)?

We prefer to avoid anything that requires full production access without a clear scope and notice period. Can you send a draft of the security exhibit with proposed limits (notice window, scope, redaction rules)? Also want to understand the proposed pen-test window and whether Redwood will provide a redacted report or full findings.

Appreciate a short call if helpful — we have availability Monday afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Alice Byrne
Head of Security, Greenline Health
alice.byrne@greenlinehealth.com

Attachments: none in initial message

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Alice Byrne <alice.byrne@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Grant <tom.grant@greenlinehealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit + audit scope questions

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. I attached a draft security exhibit that mirrors what we typically agree with our healthcare customers but with conservative guardrails. High level answers below and attached.

- SOC 2: we can provide our SOC 2 Type II report (most recent period) under NDA. We typically share the full report to the security contact and require an NDA for distribution.
- Pen test: Redwood will share a redacted executive summary and remediation attestations. For highly sensitive findings we redact IP/identifiers. We do not provide live interactive sessions into production; instead we provide logs and mitigation evidence for validated items.
- Audit access: we propose a timeboxed right: up to one in-person or remote audit per 12-month period with 14-day advance notice, conducted during business hours, limited to scoped hosts and personnel. Access will be read-only; no production writes or user data exports.
- Evidence cadence: quarterly evidence bundle (SOC 2, availability metrics, incident summary) plus ad-hoc artifacts on reasonable request with a 10-business-day turnaround.

I've attached: redlined_security_exhibit.docx (draft exhibit with track changes), SOC2-TypeII-2026.pdf (redwood copy), pen-test-summary-2026.pdf (redacted).

Proposed next step: Legal + Security sync to confirm language. Laura, can you review the exhibit and flag any absolute no-go terms for Greenline? Vanessa, FYI for deal cadence and procurement asks.

If the answers look aligned we can push a revised exhibit to procurement and request their standard NDA before sharing SOC 2. Happy to jump on a 20-min call Monday 2pm PST if that helps.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

Attachments: redlined_security_exhibit.docx; SOC2-TypeII-2026.pdf; pen-test-summary-2026.pdf

From: Alice Byrne <alice.byrne@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Grant <tom.grant@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit + audit scope questions

Priyom — thanks, that level of detail is helpful. A few follow-ups after a quick review of the attached exhibit:

1) SOC 2 sharing under NDA is acceptable. We will run the NDA through our legal team; expect a short redline.
2) The pen-test redacted summary + remediation attestations are generally fine, but procurement wants assurance that critical severity findings are not being withheld. Would Redwood consider a vetted third-party reviewer route (access to full findings under 3rd-party NDAs)?
3) Regarding audit frequency: Greenline's procurement team prefers up to two audits per year for our highest-risk vendors. Would Redwood accept limiting audits to one full-scope plus an additional remote evidence-only check annually?
4) Notice windows: procurement asked for a minimum 30-calendar-day notice rather than 14 for any on-site activity.

We're close on language; if you can confirm the third-party reviewer approach and the one full + one remote audit cadence with a 30-day notice we'll escalate to procurement and legal for signature.

Thanks,
Alice

Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Security exhibit + audit scope questions — proposed redlines and negotiation plan

Laura / Vanessa — forwarding the thread with Greenline. Procurement is pushing for 2 audits/year and a 30-day notice window. My read: we should accept the "one full-scope on-site + one remote evidence check" cadence but keep notice at 14 days for remote evidence requests and 30 days for any on-site activity. On the third-party reviewer ask, we can offer a vetted third-party reviewer option: Greenline signs the reviewer's NDA and we allow the reviewer to see full findings under a tightly scopped review agreement (no data exports, interviewer-only sessions).

Key negotiation positions I propose for Legal:
- Accept: SOC 2 Type II under NDA; redacted pen-test summary plus remediation attestations; one on-site (or remote with more privileges) + one remote evidence check per 12 months.
- Counter: require reviewer NDA + review agreement to limit distribution of full findings; production access remains read-only and subject to Redwood's change freeze windows; Redwood to redact any customer-identifiable data and sensitive IP.
- Keep: limit audit to scoped hosts/services and no live interactive prod interventions.

Please flag any language that Legal cannot concede (e.g., unlimited access, data exports, or unrestricted reproduction of SOC2). If Legal signs off on the reviewer NDA path we can move procurement to execute. Also recommend we prep a short negotiating playbook to share with the AE on acceptable concessions.

Thanks,
Priyom

-----Forwarded message attached: redlined_security_exhibit.docx (track changes)
